governance_context.executive_summary: The project builds part of the ARC genomics application and delivers QA test automation across four sequential milestones: P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, and P3 Launch. Toptal develops the micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend (React/Next.js), FastAPI services and nomenclature service on Snowflake and Azure AD/MSAL, and writes automated tests (Playwright, Jest, Pytest) for both Toptal-built and Client-built components. The Client owns platform infrastructure, the data tier, and remediation of defects in its own components.

charter.project_purpose: Build the scientist-facing ARC application within the Client's larger genomics platform and provide automated QA coverage across the full ARC program.
charter.solution_overview: The engagement delivers the scientist-facing ARC genomics application and automated QA test suites across four sequential milestones. Workstreams establish the micro-frontend shell and authentication, develop FastAPI search and direct-write services on Snowflake, build the interactive frontend with haplotype visualization, and execute comprehensive integration, performance, and UAT validation cycles.
charter.success_criteria_summary: Project success is defined by formal milestone sign-offs across all four delivery phases, sub-second search and detail API response times, and 100% passing production smoke tests with a clean 48-hour defect watch. The client receives fully tested micro-frontend and backend services integrated with Snowflake and confirmed MTA Store feature parity.
delivery_objectives: Build the micro-frontend shell with global navigation, routing, Azure AD/MSAL authentication and the Client's design system.
Implement FastAPI search, detail, asynchronous query, OneGWAS direct-write and haplotype services over Snowflake.
Build the ARC micro-frontend with faceted search, result detail and PHG/GATSBY interval visualization, plus the nomenclature service.
Deliver automated test scripts, execution and defect reports for Toptal-built and designated Client-built components.
Run integration, UAT and hardening cycles and complete production smoke testing with a 48-hour defect watch.
success_criteria: Each milestone is accepted through its own acceptance gate and sign-off, with UAT run after each milestone.
Search P95 latency under 1 second and detail P95 under 500ms.
Shell load P95 under 3 seconds and authentication success at 100%.
Frontend unit test coverage at or above 80%, with accessibility tests passing.
All critical and high defects in Toptal-built work closed and full regression green before cutover.
Production smoke tests pass 100% with a clean 48-hour defect watch.
high_level_scope: P1 Foundation (weeks 1-6): micro-frontend shell, Azure AD/MSAL authentication, end-to-end test harness, pipeline quality gates, security testing and data model validation.

P2a Services and Data (weeks 7-16): FastAPI search and detail endpoints, asynchronous query processing, performance spike, OneGWAS direct-write integration and validation of Client-built ingestion pipelines.
P2b Application Surface (weeks 17-21): ARC micro-frontend faceted search, result detail and haplotype visualization, haplotype endpoints, nomenclature service and related test suites.

P3 Launch (weeks 22-26): integration, performance, security and cross-browser (Chrome and Edge) testing, UAT execution, hardening iteration, production smoke tests, MTA Store parity confirmation and training documentation.

sow_interpretation.approval_expectations: Each milestone is an acceptance gate with its own sign-off. The client has 10 business days from notice of completion to evaluate, review, and test the Work Output (the 'Milestone Acceptance Period'), otherwise the milestone is deemed accepted (also if used in production). The client signs a milestone acceptance certification through its designated approvers (Mike Magwire and Satya). Failed items get written non-conformance details and up to three repeated remediation attempts. Dispute escalation follows Level 1 (5 business days), Level 2 (additional 5 business days), and Level 3 protocols. Hypercare includes a 30-day operational stability and warranty support period.
sow_interpretation.acceptance_process_narrative:
**Inputs ready:** Client must provide environment access, Snowflake schema deployment (HS-4781), upstream systems access (MTA, 1GWAS, GATS-B, GWAS Atlas), and design system tokens/components before dependent work proceeds. Client SME availability (Mike Magwire and Satya) is required for scheduled walkthroughs.
**Execution and tracking:** Work is organized across 5 delivery phases: P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch, and Hypercare Support. Weekly status reports track progress against user stories (HS-####) and milestone acceptance criteria, managed by Toptal Delivery Manager Saadia Iqbal.
**Submission:** Formal delivery package submitted to Client Approver Mike Magwire upon completion of each milestone with written completion notice (email suffices), initiating the Milestone Acceptance Period.
**Review:** Client has 10 business days from the completion notice to evaluate, review, and test the Work Output against specifications and Acceptance Criteria in all material respects.
**Deliverable-specific rules:** P1 Foundation requires micro-frontend shell and MSAL authentication sign-off; P2a Services and Data requires FastAPI backend and Snowflake integration (HS-4781); P2b Application Surface requires UI/UX validation and OneGWAS/GWAS Atlas workflows; P3 Launch requires production cutover, zero legacy MTA Store traffic (HS-4788), and defect resolution; Hypercare requires 30-day operational stability and warranty support.
**Triage:** If Client identifies material non-conformance, Client provides written notice specifying non-conformance details and required modifications. Non-blocking items may be triaged for subsequent sprints or Hypercare by mutual agreement.
**Remediation:** Toptal uses commercially reasonable efforts to modify non-conforming Work Output and resubmits for client acceptance.
**Rework limit:** Up to three (3) repeated remediation attempts are permitted; if unresolved within Client's reasonable discretion, contractual dispute escalation applies.
**Deemed accepted:** If Client provides no written notice of failure within the 10-business-day window or commences commercial/production use, the milestone is deemed accepted.
**Sign-off:** Mike Magwire executes and delivers written milestone acceptance certification upon successful review or deemed acceptance, authorizing milestone billing.
**Next gate:** Formal milestone sign-off acts as the contractual gateway for phase progression and invoice issuance for each fixed-fee milestone.
**Exceptions:** Scope or dependency changes (e.g. schema changes or third-party items) follow formal Change Order procedures; escalation follows Level 1 (Saadia Iqbal / Mike Magwire within 5 business days), Level 2, and Level 3 dispute protocols.

decisions.decision_text: The engagement is Fixed Fee with milestone billing, totaling $200,365 across four milestones, each invoiced on completion.
decisions.rationale: Syngenta accepted the fixed-price four-phase model. Milestone fees: $26,808 (P1), $60,356 (P2a), $68,210 (P2b), $44,991 (P3).

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf

decisions.decision_text: Delivery runs in four sequential phases (P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch). Each phase is an acceptance gate with its own deliverables, acceptance criteria and sign-off, and UAT runs after each.
decisions.rationale: The phases follow Syngenta's own plan, with P2 split on a real technical dependency boundary. Sign-off comes from Mike Magwire and Satya.

source_reference.document_name: phase-scope-and-acceptance-syngenta-arc.docx
source_reference.clause_or_slide: Section 1 (How the four phases fit together)

decisions.decision_text: Syngenta owns the platform layer (Terraform, infrastructure) and the data tier (ingestion pipelines, Snowflake data model). Toptal owns ARC application development: the micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend, FastAPI services and nomenclature service.
decisions.rationale: This ownership split was stated by Syngenta's technical lead and defines who builds, and who remediates defects in, each component.

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf

decisions.decision_text: Toptal delivers automated QA test scripts, their execution and defect reports for both Toptal-built and Syngenta-built components, rather than manual QA. Testing is against the full platform, with SSO and external integrations in test scope.
decisions.rationale: This is the position Syngenta stated. Automated scripts make test coverage durable rather than a one-off pass.

source_reference.document_name: phase-scope-and-acceptance-syngenta-arc.docx

decisions.decision_text: Toptal tests and certifies Syngenta-built components, but Syngenta remediates failures. Numeric targets on Syngenta-built work (e.g., PubMed precision, GWAS Atlas coverage, taxonomy coverage, referential integrity) are Syngenta's to achieve and are not a condition of accepting Toptal's work.
decisions.rationale: Writing a test for a component is not a guarantee that the component meets its target. Toptal re-runs scripts after remediation, and additional re-runs go through Change Order.

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf
source_reference.clause_or_slide: Exhibit A, Section 3 (Quality Assurance and Test Automation)

decisions.decision_text: A missed latency or render-time target is treated as met for Toptal's work if telemetry shows the cause is a Client-owned platform component, Client-provided third-party item, data volume or environment. The finding is logged in the defect report for Client remediation.
decisions.rationale: Toptal-built components run on Syngenta-owned Snowflake, Azure AD, CloudFront and upstream systems that Toptal does not control.

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf

decisions.decision_text: UAT is included in the fixed price and limited to two runs per milestone, covering all UAT and not only Toptal-built work. Additional runs are handled by Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Agreed on the client call to bound UAT effort within the fixed price.

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf

decisions.decision_text: Changes outside Toptal's control that force extra UAT or test cycles or test-script rework are handled by Change Order. Examples are upstream Snowflake schema changes, API taxonomy shifts, and Cogen availability below about 95%.
decisions.rationale: This protects the fixed price from rework caused by Syngenta-controlled or external changes.

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf

decisions.decision_text: Toptal will use Syngenta's existing design system for all user-facing screens. Creating, extending or maintaining the design system is excluded, and additional components or design-system changes go through Change Order.

decisions.decision_text: Test script maintenance means in-flight upkeep during development only. There is no post-launch maintenance phase, and hypercare beyond the 48-hour post-deployment defect watch is out of scope.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf, Exhibit A Section 7 and Section 8 (Third Party Items): Contract states the Cogen API is 'assumed to be available and stable at approximately 95%, as assessed by Syngenta', and failures below that level are handled by Change Order. The measurement window and method are undefined, and the contract flags Cogen/Tagasys provision as '[confirm]'.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: A client-assessed, approximate threshold gives no objective trigger for Change Orders. Unconfirmed provisioning of Cogen and Tagasys could block integration testing.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: How, over what period and by whom will Cogen availability be measured, and who provisions Cogen and Tagasys access?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: HS-4778 requires 'long queries offloaded' to an async queue, but 'long' is undefined, and the internal plan asks 'what requires the asynchronous task queue' on a platform targeting sub-second search. contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Criteria that cannot be tested objectively could be rejected or expanded after delivery, creating rework and delay.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: What query duration or condition qualifies as 'long' for async processing, and what format, scope and reviewer apply to training materials and documentation?
